subject: PHI handling & BAA request for voice transcription integration
messages:
From: Avery Cole <procurement@suncresthealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-04 09:12 -0700
Subject: PHI handling for voice-to-text integration

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for taking a look at this. We're evaluating a vendor to convert patient intake phone recordings into structured notes. A few quick questions to understand eligibility and scope:

- Will your hosted transcription pipeline ever persist raw audio or verbatim transcripts that contain PHI (names, MRNs, appointment details)?
- If so, where is that data stored and for how long? Can retention be configured per-customer?
- Do you offer a BAA for hosted transcription? If not, what are the alternative deployment options (dedicated pool / private VPC) that would allow us to put PHI through the system?
- We're also collecting SIG/CAIQ and SOC 2 evidence as part of procurement — can you provide a point-in-time SOC 2 report and a completed SIG Excel?

We'd like to get a baseline answer today and a BAA draft we can review. Proposed timeline: pilot in September if possible.

Thanks,
Avery Cole
Procurement Manager
Suncrest Health
procurement@suncresthealth.com

Attachment: none

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-04 11:05 -0700
Subject: Re: PHI handling for voice-to-text integration

Avery — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front and then next steps:

- Hosted pipeline: by default we do not treat audio or transcripts as PHI on ingestion; we persist transcripts in encrypted object storage for up to 7 days (configurable). That default is meant for non-sensitive workloads.
- BAA: we do offer a BAA, but it depends on the deployment mode. Hosted customers can be covered under our standard BAA with specific controls (encryption at rest, access controls, audit logging). For higher-assurance needs we recommend Dedicated or Private where we can guarantee isolation and customer-managed keys.
- Retention: retention is configurable per-customer; we can set aggressive deletion and retention policies or provide a one-time purge.
- Evidence: we can share a recent SOC 2 report and a completed SIG spreadsheet.

I'm attaching a short "Redwood HIPAA quick guide" that summarizes options and where PHI is allowed vs not allowed. Next step: Monica (CS) will share a BAA draft and a dataflow diagram for your security team. Dev will be on the thread for technical questions.

Are you able to share an example recording that contains typical fields (with identifiers redacted) so we can size the pipeline? Also, do you expect live streaming (real-time) or batched uploads?

Best,
Marcus Lin

Hi Avery — attaching the items Marcus promised.

Summary of what we're sending:
- Draft BAA (BAA-draft-for-prospects.docx) — this is our standard customer-facing draft; legal can produce a more limited "pilot BAA" if you prefer to run a short test.
- Transcription dataflow diagram (transcription-dataflow-diagram.png) — shows where audio and transcripts travel in our hosted, dedicated, and private options.
- A one-page checklist with configuration options (retention, KMS key ownership, transcript redaction hooks).

Notes and clarifications:
- Hosted: transcripts and audio can be configured to auto-delete after X hours; access is audited. Hosted is eligible for a standard BAA but some customers prefer Dedicated for PHI to avoid multi-tenant storage for raw audio.
- Dedicated: isolated GPU pools, optional customer-managed KMS, and ability to disable transcript persistence entirely (streaming-only path).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full isolation and can be configured for air-gapped retention or on-prem storage.

I'll leave this with Legal to surface the BAA tailoring options. If Suncrest wants a scoped pilot, we can provide a limited BAA and a time-boxed dedicated environment for the trial.

Monica / Marcus — thanks for the materials. A few follow-ups from our security and legal review after an initial pass:

1) BAA scope: we'd like to see explicit clauses for (a) ephemeral transcripts (how deletion is enforced), (b) forensic audit logs for access to PHI, and (c) SLA on secure deletion within X hours after request. Can you indicate which of those are standard vs. negotiable?

2) KMS: we prefer customer-managed keys (CMK) for any PHI in storage. For hosted customers, is CMK supported? If not, what compensating controls exist?

3) Evidence: please provide a link to a current SOC 2 Type II report (not redacted cover letter only) and a completed SIG/CAIQ. We've attached our Suncrest SIG template for you to complete (Suncrest-SIG.xlsx).

4) Deployment: cost and timing for a 30-day dedicated trial (isolated pool) — high-level estimate will suffice for procurement planning.

5) Live transcription: if we route live streams, will you be able to ensure transcripts are never written to long-term storage? We need a technical statement.

Can we set a call early next week with engineering? We want to finalize a pilot SOW by the end of the month.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Senior Counsel — Privacy & Security
Suncrest Health
legal@suncresthealth.com

Lena / Avery — appreciate the precise asks. Quick clarifications and proposed next steps so we can keep procurement moving: 

- BAA clauses: we can commit to audited access logs and a deletion SLA of 24 hours for transcripts when deletion is requested (configurable down to 0 hours for dedicated/private). We'll flag the deletion clause as negotiable; CMK support for hosted is limited today but possible via a partner gateway — otherwise Dedicated/Private supports CMK out of the box.
- Live streaming: we have a streaming-only path where tokens flow through memory and the KV cache is disabled; transcripts are not persisted. We'll provide a technical note and proof-of-concept run for your engineers.
- SOC 2 & SIG: links below. The SOC 2 Type II PDF is available for signed NDAs; we can provide it today if you sign our standard NDA. The completed SIG template (Suncrest-SIG.xlsx) will be returned within 48 hours.

Links / attachments:
